issues.description: Class name/type inconsistency for the shared stock component: the problem statement and UML declare a class named 'Stock' (and describe SealSaloon.stock as being of type Stock and related static methods that manage it). The template and solution repositories do not implement a 'Stock' class; instead they provide an implemented class named 'Inventory' that exposes the methods and behavior described for 'Stock' (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). An empty Stock.java file is present in both template and solution. SealSaloon in the solution uses Inventory as the static stock field. This mismatch (problem statement/UML -> 'Stock' vs template/solution -> 'Inventory') makes it unclear which class name students should use when implementing SealSaloon.stock and related static methods and may cause them to implement or modify the wrong class or leave an unused empty Stock.java file.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the class name used for the shared stock across all artifacts. Either: (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' everywhere (so students implement/use Inventory as provided), or (B) rename the provided Inventory.java to Stock.java (remove the empty Stock.java), and update SealSaloon and any references to use the Stock type. Ensure the UML, textual description, template files, and solution tests all consistently use the same class name so students know which type to use for the shared stock attribute.

issues.description: The exercise description and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (methods: add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) while the provided codebase declares and implements this concept as class 'Inventory' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java). Additionally, there is an empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java file in both template and solution repositories, and SealSaloon in the solution references a static field of type Inventory (private static final Inventory stock = new Inventory()). This mismatch means: the problem statement/UML calls the conceptual entity 'Stock', the template/solution code exposes it as 'Inventory', and an empty Stock.java file remains in the project. Students reading the UML or instructions will look for a 'Stock' class to use or implement, but the working implementation is named 'Inventory', which is inconsistent and likely to cause confusion or extra search time.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the shared inventory concept across all artifacts. Either: (A) rename the Inventory class and its file to Stock (change class name to 'Stock', file name to Stock.java, and update all references in SealSaloon and other files), and remove the empty Stock.java duplicates; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' everywhere instead of 'Stock' and remove the empty Stock.java file(s). Ensure the public API matches the UML: methods add(String), take(String), findStockIngredient(String), addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), emptyStock().
